verdicts.claim: By default every connection runs an automatic checkpoint after any COMMIT that leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more (compile-time option SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT)
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more'; wal_autocheckpoint: checkpoints it starts are PASSIVE

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE copies as many frames as it can without waiting and never invokes the busy handler. FULL takes the writer lock (blocking new writers but not new readers)
verdicts.evidence: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode'; FULL 'blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row with three integers: busy, log, and checkpointed... Both counts are -1 if not WAL mode, both 0 after successful TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: v2 page: after successful TRUNCATE 'both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'; pragma: 'second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'

verdicts.claim: Every checkpoint takes the exclusive WAL_CKPT_LOCK... returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately and does not invoke the busy handler; nBackfill may only increase while WAL_CKPT_LOCK held
verdicts.evidence: v2: 'Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case'; walformat: 'The nBackfill can only be increased while holding the WAL_CKPT_LOCK'

verdicts.claim: The wal-index keeps five read marks; a reader holding WAL_READ_LOCK(N) limits backfill to the first read-mark[N] frames
verdicts.evidence: 'Five read marks'; checkpoint 'must not move WAL content into the main database for more than the first read-mark[N] frames'

verdicts.claim: A writer may reset the WAL when nBackfill equals mxFrame and no connection holds WAL_READ_LOCK(1) through WAL_READ_LOCK(4)
verdicts.evidence: 'it is ok to reset the WAL if there are no locks held on any of WAL_READ_LOCK(N) for N>0'

verdicts.claim: With synchronous=NORMAL in WAL mode, ordinary commits do not sync. SQLite syncs the WAL before each checkpoint, the database file after each completed checkpoint
verdicts.evidence: pragma: 'the WAL file is synchronized before each checkpoint'; 'With synchronous=FULL in WAL mode, an additional sync operation of the WAL file happens after each transaction commit'

verdicts.claim: Checkpoints do not shrink the -wal file... overwriting is faster than appending... journal_size_limit (default -1, no limit)
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'normally faster to overwrite an existing file than to append'; pragma: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)'

verdicts.claim: SQLite says its 1000-page default 'seems to work well in test applications on workstations'
verdicts.evidence: 'this strategy seems to work well in test applications on workstations'

verdicts.claim: The checkpointer writes pages in ascending page-number order to keep writes sequential, but seeks remain, so a checkpoint is slower than a write transaction
verdicts.evidence: 'the pages are transferred from WAL to database in ascending order... These factors combine to make checkpoints slower than write transactions'

verdicts.claim: Only the newest copy of each page in the WAL needs to be written
verdicts.evidence: fly.io: 'copies the latest version of each page in the WAL back'; 'prior versions of page 2 are ignored'

verdicts.claim: In the WAL-reset race the writer's reset increments the WAL salt... The fix compares the live WAL header salt with the copy it took at checkpoint start
verdicts.evidence: Canonical: fix checks 'that the wal has not been wrapped since the header was read for this checkpoint' by comparing live salt with salt copied at start (Eaton post does not describe the fix)

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE, added in 3.16.0 (2017-01-02), disables the close-time checkpoint
verdicts.evidence: 3.16.0 (2017-01-02): 'Added the SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE option to sqlite3_db_config()'

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug is likely present in SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). Dan found and fixed it on 2026-03-03; 3.51.3 (2026-03-13); backports 3.44.6, 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'; 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed'

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug requires WAL mode and two or more connections open on the same database file, in separate threads or processes
verdicts.evidence: 'two or more database connections open on the same file, in separate threads or processes, and when those two connections attempt to write or checkpoint at the same instant'

verdicts.claim: SQLite 3.52.0 (2026-03-06) was withdrawn and its planned features moved to 3.53.0 (2026-04-09). 3.53.0 also lists the WAL-reset fix
verdicts.evidence: 3.52.0 page: Withdrawn, 'features... moved forward into version 3.53.0'; 3.53.0 (2026-04-09): 'Fix the WAL-reset database corruption bug'

verdicts.claim: SQLite 3.51.0 (2025-11-04) added PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP mode
verdicts.evidence: 3.51.0 item 7: 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument'

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE arrived in SQLite 3.8.8 (2015-01-16), and 3.8.8.2 (2015-01-30) fixed it so that it actually truncates
verdicts.evidence: 3.8.8 (2015-01-16) adds SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE; 3.8.8.2 (2015-01-30) 'truncates the WAL file even if there is no checkpoint work to be done'

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5.x runs PASSIVE checkpoints at min-checkpoint-page-count (default 1000) and every checkpoint-interval (default 1m). truncate-page-n default 121359
verdicts.evidence: min-checkpoint-page-count 1000 '~4MB'; checkpoint-interval 'Default: 1 minute'; truncate-page-n 121359 '~500MB'; passive-first since v0.5.15

verdicts.claim: Litestream recommends PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0... tens of thousands of small writes per second... busy_timeout=5000
verdicts.evidence: 'It is recommended to set this to 5 seconds'; 'many small write transactions (e.g. tens of thousands per second)'; 'takes a fresh full snapshot'

verdicts.claim: Litestream holds a long-running read transaction so no other process can checkpoint and restart the WAL; LTX files (v0.5; v0.3 used shadow WAL)
verdicts.evidence: 'starts a long-running read transaction to prevent any other process from checkpointing and restarting the WAL file'; v0.3.x used 'a directory of shadow WAL files'

verdicts.claim: Litestream logs 'passive checkpoint skipped' when SQLITE_BUSY is returned
verdicts.evidence: PASSIVE 'returns SQLITE_BUSY if readers or writers are active'; Litestream logs 'passive checkpoint skipped'

verdicts.claim: sqlite3_wal_hook() registers one callback per connection... after the write lock is released... NULL hook disables automatic checkpoints
verdicts.evidence: 'at most a single write-ahead log callback'; 'Passing a NULL pointer for the callback disables automatic checkpointing entirely'

verdicts.claim: rqlite disables SQLite autocheckpointing and checkpoint-on-close... TRUNCATE checkpoint at each Raft snapshot... v10 250 ms wait... compares WAL salt values
verdicts.evidence: O'Toole (2026-05-12): disables checkpoint-on-close, TRUNCATE at Raft snapshot, waits up to 250 ms then aborts/retries, records salt values; dbconfig: 'zero (the default) to enable them'

verdicts.claim: Rails 7.1 (October 2023) changed its SQLite defaults to journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL and journal_size_limit=64MB
verdicts.evidence: BigBinary (2023-10-31): WAL, synchronous NORMAL, 'journal_size_limit is now capped at 64MB'; page does not state the Rails 7.1 release date itself

verdicts.claim: The Rails SQLite3Adapter DEFAULT_PRAGMAS (main branch) set journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL and journal_size_limit=67108864 (64 MB), and leave wal_autocheckpoint
verdicts.evidence: "journal_size_limit" => 67108864, # 64 megabytes; wal_autocheckpoint not set

verdicts.claim: The wal2 journal mode, available only on a SQLite development branch, alternates writers between <db>-wal and <db>-wal2... SQLITE_NOTADB... must switch to delete
verdicts.evidence: 'Attempting to use any other version of SQLite results in an SQLITE_NOTADB error'; 'not possible to change a database directly from wal mode to wal2 mode'

verdicts.claim: In February 2026 Syncthing kept SQLite auto-checkpoint enabled and added a timer-based checkpointer... hours-long transactions pinned WAL pages
verdicts.evidence: 2026-02-06: 'We don't disable the auto checkpoint functionality'; 'If a transaction is open for hours'; 'we're blocking our own checkpointer'; 'multiple gigabytes'

verdicts.claim: VACUUM on a WAL-mode database writes the rebuilt database through the WAL... run PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) right after VACUUM
verdicts.evidence: 'The entire rebuilt database gets written to the WAL file'; journal_size_limit 'does NOT prevent WAL growth during VACUUM'; 'Always use checkpoint(TRUNCATE) after VACUUM'

verdicts.claim: Very large write transactions fit WAL poorly... SQLite says rollback-journal modes are likely faster for transactions larger than about 100 MB
verdicts.evidence: wal.html states the 100 MB line but the same paragraph says: 'Beginning with version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), WAL mode works as efficiently with large transactions as does rollback mode' — claim omits that the guidance is pre-3.11.0

verdicts.claim: A prepared statement that has not been reset keeps its connection's read transaction open... COMMIT only downgrades... Python cursor.execute() without fetchall()
verdicts.evidence: Hipp: COMMIT 'does not cancel a pending read transaction'; OP: cursor.execute without fetchall() left statement pending; 2022 thread: step to SQLITE_DONE or sqlite3_reset()

verdicts.claim: Richard Hipp gave this diagnosis in 2021 for a user whose WAL had grown to about 100 GB
verdicts.evidence: 2021-04-06: 'Currently the WAL-File is about 100GB'; Hipp: unreset statements leave 'some transactions open, which will prevent the checkpoint'

verdicts.claim: In a 2021 SQLite Forum case with 36 connections and about 1000 writes per second, setting PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0 on every connection made RESTART succeed
verdicts.evidence: 2021-09-26: '36 connections', 'about 1000 writes per second', 'Setting PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0; on every connection resolves the issue'

verdicts.claim: sqlite3_setlk_timeout() (added in 3.50.0) with the SQLITE_SETLK_BLOCK_ON_CONNECT flag makes the new connection wait instead
verdicts.evidence: 3.50.0 (2025-05-29) adds 'sqlite3_setlk_timeout() interface'; setlk page: new reader 'fails with an SQLITE_BUSY error' unless SQLITE_SETLK_BLOCK_ON_CONNECT

verdicts.claim: The newest release on 2026-10-16 is 3.54.1
verdicts.evidence: changes.html lists 3.54.1 at top dated 2026-10-16

verdicts.claim: Phil Eaton's reproducer (2026-08-23) is about 100 lines of C using only the public API: two threads and three connections... 1 GiB mmap_size
verdicts.evidence: ~100 lines C, public API, two threads three connections, passive checkpoints, 1 GiB mmap_size, 'database disk image is malformed' on 3.51.2

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA integrity_check does not detect every WAL-reset loss... although it did catch the corruption in Tailscale's databases. Tailscale found vanished data via its transaction log
verdicts.evidence: Eaton: lost-write run reported 'integrity_check: ok' and notes integrity check catching Tailscale's corruption was partly luck; the 'own transaction log' detail was not found in Techzine (unconfirmed sub-point)

verdicts.claim: Antithesis (2026-08-12) found it in 15 minutes on 3.51.2 with a generic workload... the same run passed on 3.51.3
verdicts.evidence: dated August 12, 2026: 'Antithesis caught the bug in 15 mins'; '3.51.3 comes back clean'

verdicts.claim: Tailscale reported 19 SQLite database corruptions over about six months, starting with a corrupted backup flagged in August 2025... tmstmpvfs
verdicts.evidence: Gigazine: '19 database corruptions in six months', S3 backup corruption that August, 'logs left by the tmstmpvfs shim'

verdicts.claim: According to Techzine, SQLite 3.52.0 (2026-03-06) shipped the WAL-reset fix first... floating-point rounding change made existing indexes report false corruption
verdicts.evidence: Techzine: first fix shipped in 3.52.0, false corruption alarms in 13 databases from floating-point rounding change; news.html: 3.52.0 withdrawn

verdicts.claim: Tailscale took 'manual control of the checkpoint process' so it could run fast, consistent backups at its 'own aggressive pace'
verdicts.evidence: Register: 'running at our own aggressive pace'; 'Most people use SQLite in a standard configuration and never face this sort of issue'
